standard: NFPA 13 (2019 edition) - Hazen-Williams C values for sprinkler piping; C/epsilon pairings per Table A.27.2.4.8.2 (Suggested Epsilon-Factor for Aged Pipe)
note: systemType ANY means the value does not vary with wet/dry/preaction service. A caller may always override C per pipe segment; this table is the reference/default set. epsilonFactor is the equivalent absolute roughness NFPA 13's annex pairs with each C value -- recorded for reference only, since this package uses Hazen-Williams (which takes C, not roughness). Nothing in calc-core reads it today; mechanical.pipe's Darcy-Weisbach path gets its roughness from reference/pipes/*.json instead.
annexNote: Table A.27.2.4.8.2 also lists steel (new) at C=143 / epsilon 0.0018 in. This app does not expose that row: NFPA 13 design practice uses the aged values (120 wet, 100 dry), and 'new vs aged' is a pipe-age dimension this table is not keyed on. Its epsilon of 0.045 mm does match reference/pipes/bi.json's absoluteRoughnessMm, which is the Darcy-Weisbach figure the pipe package uses.

cFactors.label: Steel - wet system
cFactors.sourceNote: Table A.27.2.4.8.2 'Steel' row, C=120. Unlined steel pipe in a wet system.

cFactors.label: Steel - dry system
cFactors.sourceNote: Table A.27.2.4.8.2 'Steel' row, C=100. The lower C than wet service accounts for internal corrosion in dry/alternating pipe.

cFactors.label: Steel - preaction system
cFactors.sourceNote: C=100 itself is the published Table A.27.2.4.8.2 value, but treating preaction as dry service is this application's mapping, not something the table states.

cFactors.label: CPVC (listed sprinkler pipe)
cFactors.sourceNote: Table A.27.2.4.8.2 lists 'Plastic' at C=150; reading CPVC as that row is this application's mapping. A specific listed CPVC product's C comes from its listing.

cFactors.label: Ductile iron - cement lined, underground
cFactors.sourceNote: Not listed in Table A.27.2.4.8.2; entered from general knowledge of underground supply mains and still needs a source.
